overview.title: Water and quiet a short ride from town
overview.p1: Dayet Aoua is the lake most visitors pair with Ifrane. It sits on the plateau with a path around the water, seasonal birdlife and open views toward the forested ridges.
overview.p2: Come for a walk, a picnic and photos rather than swimming infrastructure. Levels and access can vary with rainfall — ask locally if the path is fully open.
overview.p3: Morning is best for birds and soft light. Combine with the cedar forest the same day if you have a car or driver.

q1.question: How far from Ifrane?
q1.answer: About 15–20 minutes by car depending on the route.

q2.question: Entry fee?
q2.answer: Generally free public access; confirm any local parking charge.

q3.question: Swimming?
q3.answer: Not the main activity — treat it as a walk and picnic lake.

q4.question: Best season?
q4.answer: Spring and autumn for mild weather; winter can be cold and wet.

q5.question: Combine with?
q5.answer: Cedar forest or return to Ifrane for dinner.

food.title: Eat at the lake
food.p1: Bring a picnic. Facilities are limited compared with a town restaurant.
food.p2: Pack out all rubbish — the plateau stays beautiful when visitors leave no trace.
